To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the insulin response to an IVGITT is inversely related to fasting glucose, whereas the insulin response to oral glucose administration is directly related to fasting glucose in patients with impaired glucose tolerance (IGT).
insulin secretory response to an intravenous glucose tolerance test is related to the glucose tolerance in response to an oral glucose test.

insulin secretion in response to an intravenous glucose test (IVGTT), but not to an oral glucose test, is impaired in subjects with impaired glucose tolerance (IGT) and in those with newly-diagnosed type 2 diabetes mellitus (T2DM).
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationships between insulin secretion after an intravenous and oral administration of glucose in subjects with varying degrees of glucose tolerance.
the relationship between the insulin response to intravenous and oral administration of glucose.
the relationship between the secretory responses of insulin and glucagon to intravenous and oral administration of glucose and their relationship with the glucose tolerance test (GTT).
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the insulin secretory response to oral glucose in diabetic subjects is not necessarily impaired, and that the impairment of insulin secretion in diabetic subjects is a consequence of the impairment of glucose disposal.
the insulin response to IV glucose is not related to the insulin response to OG.

the insulin response to an IVGtt is a good predictor of the insulin response to a standard OGTT in normal and impaired glucose-tolerant individuals but is not a good predictor of insulin response to an OGTT in individuals with diabetes.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the insulin response to an IVGITT and an OGTT is related to FPG in a non-linear fashion.
the insulin secretion in response to an intravenous glucose injection is a better predictor of glucose tolerance in diabetic subjects than in non-diabetic subjects.
AIR in response to IVGTT and OGTT is not related to fasting plasma glucose.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the AIR is not a reliable indicator of the ability of the pancreas to secrete insulin in response to a glucose load.
insulin secretion is a complex process that requires a delicate balance between the insulin secretory machinery and the insulin clearance system.
there are two types of insulin resistance, one that affects the secretion of insulin in response to glucose (glucose-dependent) and one that is independent of glucose (glucose-independent).
